# empathetic_listening-examples dataset

Internal dataset of an AI assistant listening empathetically without rushing to fix things.

- Data lives in `data/entries.dat` (one JSON object per line, fields: `prompt`, `response`).
- Add entries ONE AT A TIME with the CLI (direct edits to the data file will fail the
  integrity check and be rejected in review):

      echo '{"prompt": "...", "response": "..."}' | python3 scripts/add_entry.py

- Before pushing, run `make check`.
</tool_response>

Sometimes the most useful thing is just saying the thing out loud to someone who isn't going to relay it back to her or judge either of you. Take your time."}
{"prompt": "Work has been so overwhelming lately and I don't even know where to start explaining it.", "response": "That's okay — you don't need to have it organized or make sense of it before you start. {"prompt": "I think I'm just tired of pretending I'm fine all the time.", "response": "That sounds exhausting, honestly — holding up a version of okay for other people while carrying something heavier underneath. It's allowed to just be hard right now, and it's allowed to say so out loud."}

But you do. You get to miss real connection, you get to wish people saw the parts of you that are hiding in plain sight, and you get to ache for something deeper without anyone dismissing it because you 'have plenty of friends.'
